title: POC scoping - Sable Systems (open model shortlist)
summary: Initial POC scoping for Sable Systems focusing on open-model shortlist and tradeoffs. Key success criteria: 95th pct latency under 600ms for short prompts, accuracy on domain QA >= 88% (human eval), cost target <$0.002 per 1k tokens. Workload: 1000-2k RPM steady, spikes to 6k. POC timeline proposed 3 weeks of benchmarks + 3 weeks integration. Models shortlisted: Llama 3 (13B), Mistral Instruct, Mistral 7B-v2, Falcon-40B-Inst (quantized variants), RedPajama-Instruct variants. Multilingual requirements (EN/FR/ES), legal domain Q&A dataset. Security: need VPC peering option and KMS integration; Redwood to share security pack and SOC2 attestation.
next_steps: Redwood to send security docs + SOC2 report (Evan) by 2027-07-23
Redwood to provision benchmark cluster and share runbook (Priya) by 2027-07-26
Sable to provide 500 representative test prompts and domain dataset (Dana) by 2027-07-24
action_items: Evan: send security docs and pricing sheet (due 2027-07-23)
Priya: share benchmark runbook + test harness template (due 2027-07-26)
Dana: share sample domain dataset and rubric (due 2027-07-24)
Marco: confirm VPC peering windows and credential churn policy (due 2027-07-25)
transcript:
[00:00] Evan Morris: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Evan from Redwood, I'm the AE on this. Priya and I are here to scope the POC for open model selection.
[00:08] Dana Lee: Hi all, Dana here. Thanks, Evan. We're excited to get this moving — main ask is to pick a model that balances cost and domain accuracy for our legal QA assistant.
[00:18] Priya Shah: Hi Dana, Marco, Aisha — Priya from Redwood SE. Quick agenda: success criteria, workload sizing, bench metric targets, shortlist models and tradeoffs, timeline. Does that work?
[00:28] Marco Ruiz: Yep. Also, quick note — security is a blocker for us; we need a VPC option and KMS integration, and we'll want to review SOC 2.
[00:36] Evan Morris: Absolutely, we can share SOC 2 and our security pack after the call.
[00:40] Aisha Khan: One more thing, we will need French and Spanish support — not full parity but reasonable fidelity for customer-facing responses.
[00:48] Priya Shah: Ok great, multilingual included. Let's start with success criteria — what will make the POC a win for you?
[00:55] Dana Lee: Win = model that answers legal Qs with high factual accuracy and low hallucination. For numbers: target ~88% correct on our eval set (human-reviewed) and under 5% critical hallucinations. Latency target is softer but we want 95th percentile < 600ms for typical short prompts (up to 128 tokens). Cost target ideally below $0.002 per 1k tokens — that's a ballpark.
[01:20] Priya Shah: Helpful — so accuracy (88%+), hallucination threshold, P95 latency <600ms, and cost target. For the POC we'll measure human-eval accuracy and automated metrics (ROUGE/BLEU less useful here), and we'll run latency/cost per token.
[01:32] Marco Ruiz: Also we expect around 1k to 2k RPM steady state per region, with spikes up to 6k RPM for heavy days. Token distribution: median request ~80 tokens, max ~1024 for a few tasks.
[01:44] Evan Morris: Noted. That workload shape favors batching and prefix cache for repeated templates. We'll size cluster for both steady and spike.
[01:50] Dana Lee: Ok on metrics. Now model shortlist — we prefer open models to avoid vendor lock. Thoughts?
[01:57] Priya Shah: For open models, shortlist I'd recommend: Llama 3 13B (if you want instruction tuned and strong zero-shot), Mistral Instruct (7B-v2 and the larger family), Falcon-40B-Inst (we often test quantized L4/INT8 variants), and RedPajama-Instruct 7B/15B variants. We'll also test Llama 2 13B as a baseline.
[02:15] Aisha Khan: How do they stack in multilingual and legal domain?
[02:18] Priya Shah: Quick tradeoffs — Llama 3 generally good across EU languages, solid instruction tuning. Mistral is cost-efficient and surprisingly strong on reasoning; 7B-v2 is good for cheaper inference. Falcon-40B tends to be higher quality out-of-the-box but bigger and costlier; quantization (int8) helps but sometimes impacts subtle legal phrasing. RedPajama family is competitive and easier to finetune. Llama 2 sometimes trails on multilinguals depending on variant.
[02:41] Marco Ruiz: Quantization worry — does INT8/4 materially change hallucination rate?
[02:45] Priya Shah: Sometimes, yes. We've seen small drops in factuality when aggressively quantized for long-form generations; for short QA it's usually ok but needs to be measured. For legal domain nuance, we'd include both full-precision (fp16) and int8 runs in the POC.
[03:00] Dana Lee: For cost modeling, can Redwood show per-token cost for each model variant including batching and cache effects?
[03:06] Evan Morris: Yes — Priya will run benchmark apples-to-apples: same prompts, same hardware profile, and we'll estimate cost per 1k tokens with realistic batching. We'll share a spreadsheet.
[03:14] Aisha Khan: On multilingual — we need EN/FR/ES. Do we need different models per language or single model can handle all?
[03:21] Priya Shah: Many instruction-tuned models handle multiple languages, but there are quality deltas. We'll run our multilingual eval subset; if a smaller model struggles we can recommend a larger single model or language-specialized small models. Tradeoff is operational complexity vs cost/quality.
[03:36] Marco Ruiz: Any security constraints for the POC infra? We want data not to leave our VPC and keys managed by our KMS.
[03:43] Evan Morris: For Private deployment we can do a customer-managed control plane; for Dedicated we support VPC peering and KMS. For hosted POC we can do encrypted at rest with bring-your-own-key options for enterprise trials. We'll share the VPC runbook.
[03:58] Dana Lee: Timeline — what does a POC look like?
[04:02] Priya Shah: Proposed: week 0 (this week) - kickoff and dataset exchange. Week 1 - benchmark configuration and runs (fp16 + int8 for 3-4 model variants). Week 2 - human eval and error analysis; mid-week demo. Week 3 - integration prototype (API wired into your staging UI) and final readout. We usually budget 3-4 weeks; you might want a slightly longer integration window.
[04:25] Marco Ruiz: That aligns. We should allow a week extra for security review if needed.
[04:29] Evan Morris: Fine. So practically we'll provision a small Dedicated cluster in our hosted lab and run 2-3 parallel model builds. Priya, can you describe bench metrics you'll collect?
[04:38] Priya Shah: Sure: P50/P95 latency for 1-32 token generation and 128-token gen, throughput (RPS) under batching rules, token-per-second GPU throughput, cost per 1k tokens estimated, and automated accuracy metrics plus human eval results (binary correctness + hallucination flags). We'll also measure memory/kv cache footprint to determine feasible concurrency.
[05:00] Dana Lee: On human eval, we'll provide a rubric and 500 prompts. How many annotators do you typically use?
[05:07] Priya Shah: We can do an internal quick eval (2 annotators) for initial numbers and you can do a final 3rd-party review if you prefer. For POC we aim for consistency rather than production-grade labeling.
[05:18] Aisha Khan: Can we test retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) during POC? We want the model to cite statutes and our internal policy docs.
[05:26] Priya Shah: Yes — include a RAG pass in one of the runs: vector store + top-k retrieval, then feed context into model. That will change latency and token counts; we'll model both naive and cached RAG.
[05:35] Evan Morris: Quick note on model-sizing: given your spike pattern, we recommend testing with an initial cluster that can handle 6k RPM with 80-token median using batching; we'll show cost delta for dedicated GPUs vs hosted burst.
[05:47] Marco Ruiz: What hardware would you use for the fp16 runs? A100s? And for cheaper runs, GA100 or L40s?
[05:53] Priya Shah: We'll run fp16 on A100-style hardware in the testbed for consistent kernel perf; for cost-targets we'll emulate commodity GPUs and show quantized runs on more cost-efficient accelerators. We'll annotate the spreadsheet for hardware assumptions.
[06:06] Dana Lee: Any gotchas on instruction tuning or prompt templates for legal domain?
[06:10] Priya Shah: Yes — prompt engineering matters a lot. We'll test a few canonical templates (instruction, chain-of-thought off, answer with citations). Sometimes enabling chain-of-thought reduces correctness on short QA; we'll test both. For legal specificity, small finetune or retrieval augmentation often helps more than larger models.
[06:28] Aisha Khan: Good — we prefer RAG + smaller model if quality is close, but willing to pick a larger model if accuracy gap >5 points.
[06:35] Priya Shah: Sounds like a clear decision rule: if accuracy delta between smaller (e.g., Mistral 7B-v2/int8) and larger (Llama 3 13B or Falcon-40B) is >5% on your rubric, recommend larger; else recommend smaller with RAG. We'll codify that in the readout.
[06:50] Evan Morris: Any regulatory constraints? Dana?
[06:53] Dana Lee: We can't persist PII in logs; if PII appears it must be redacted, and audit logs required. Also need RBAC and SSO.
[07:02] Evan Morris: We support audit logs and RBAC; SSO SAML supported. We'll include that in the security pack.
[07:06] Marco Ruiz: On benchmarks, are you able to include a baseline using our current model? We have an internal OpenAI deployment right now.
[07:12] Priya Shah: Yes please send a few sample responses or metric sheet. We'll include baseline numbers in the spreadsheet to show delta.
[07:19] Dana Lee: We'll supply a short baseline CSV with response samples and timing from our current infra.
[07:24] Evan Morris: Great. Any other concerns?
[07:26] Aisha Khan: Pricing — after the POC, if we go production, what's the commit minimum for Dedicated?
[07:31] Evan Morris: That depends on region and GPU type; we'll provide a tiered proposal in the pricing sheet. For early-stage POCs we often do a month-to-month pilot on dedicated pools before committing.
[07:42] Marco Ruiz: Ok. One more technical — will Redwood's runtime expose logs at token granularity for debugging?
[07:48] Priya Shah: We expose structured traces, token-level timing for debug builds, and sampling of outputs. Full token dumps are possible under enterprise agreements; we can redact PII as needed.
[07:59] Dana Lee: Good. Let's recap next steps.
[08:01] Evan Morris: Recap: Evan sends security pack + SOC2 by Friday. Priya to provision benchmark cluster and run initial fp16 + int8 tests on the shortlist (Llama 3 13B, Mistral 7B-v2, Falcon-40B-Inst quant, RedPajama 15B) and share runbook. Sable provides 500 prompts and baseline CSV. Schedule kickoff run on Tuesday 2027-07-27 at 09:00 PT.
[08:23] Aisha Khan: Sounds good.
[08:25] Marco Ruiz: Thanks, talk soon.
[08:27] Priya Shah: Thanks everyone.
[08:29] Evan Morris: Thanks — we'll follow up with calendar invite and docs.
[08:33] [call end]
